text:
The evidence can't say what caused the loss. It shows that it happened, but not why.

What it shows: Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022 within the asset, which is 3.41% of its 17.6 ha. The JRC 2020 map agrees the area was forest, and a later year (up to 2025) was observed. Per the MGAP 2021 map, about 0.5 ha was native forest and 0.1 ha was outside mapped forest. No planted forest was involved. A further 0.2 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

What it doesn't show: Hansen loss captures any stand replacement, so it can't distinguish harvest, fire, storm, or clearing. It also doesn't establish whether land use changed, whether the change was authorized, who was responsible, or any compliance status such as EUDR.

To find the cause, you would need other evidence, such as field records, permits, or fire or storm data.
